newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel oil bid up by one buyer.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel oil bid up by one buyer.

text.p: NWE high sulphur fuel oil barges jumped to $90 fob a tonne on Monday with last week's dominant buyer again bidding up values aggressively, traders said.
Some 11-12,000 tonnes was bought at $89 and another 1-2,000 at $90, up $2 from Friday, in what was otherwise a quiet market.
"Normally there would be no reason for prices to go up, there is plenty of fuel oil out there," said one refiner. "The buyer wants to see $90 in the market."
Fundamentals were more clearly reflected in the cargo market where prices held firm at $82/$84 cif, traders said, and demand remained very weak.
Dealers described both the low and high sulphur cargo markets as dead, with little movement in price despite higher swaps and crude futures.
Tight supply and the pickup in paper values pushed up prices on the low sulphur barge market. Offers were $96 on Friday and $95 today, with bids around $93.
